species.name: Ramps (wild leeks)
species.identify: Two or three smooth, flat, lily-like leaves rising from a single reddish stalk, and an unmistakable onion-garlic smell when crushed. If it does not smell of onion, it is not a ramp.

species.name: Fiddleheads (ostrich fern)
species.identify: Tight bright-green coils with a deep U-shaped groove on the inside of a smooth stem, wrapped in papery brown scales that rub off. No fuzz.

species.name: Morels
species.identify: Honeycomb pitted cap fused to the stem, and completely hollow from cap tip to stem base when sliced lengthwise.

species.name: Stinging nettle
species.identify: Opposite, deeply toothed, heart-based leaves on a square stem, covered in stinging hairs. The sting is the identification.

species.name: Dandelion
species.identify: A basal rosette of jagged, backward-pointing lobes, a hollow leafless stalk with milky sap, and one flower per stalk.

species.name: Wild asparagus
species.identify: In spring, familiar spears. Find the patch in fall instead: tall feathery ferns with red berries mark exactly where to return.

species.name: Spruce and fir tips
species.identify: The new growth at branch tips in late spring: pale bright green, soft, still wearing a papery brown sheath.

species.name: Cattail shoots
species.identify: Tall, flat, strap-like leaves wrapping a round, spongy base, often beside last year's brown spikes; peel the inner shoot from the base for the white 'Cossack asparagus'.

species.name: Wild violets
species.identify: Heart-shaped leaves and five-petalled purple flowers, each on its own leafless stalk straight from the ground.

species.name: Wild strawberry
species.identify: Three toothed leaflets, white five-petalled flowers, and a small red berry with seeds sitting in tiny pits on the surface.

species.name: Serviceberry (saskatoon)
species.identify: A shrub or small tree with oval, toothed leaves; berries look like small blueberries but carry a tiny five-pointed crown at the tip and have soft seeds inside.

species.name: Mulberries
species.identify: Blackberry-shaped fruit growing on a tree, not a cane. Leaves vary wildly on one tree, from plain ovals to mitten shapes. Most wild mulberries are the introduced white mulberry, whose ripe fruit may be white, pink or black; the native red mulberry is rare in Canada.

species.name: Elderflower
species.identify: Big flat-topped creamy flower heads on a woody, many-stemmed shrub with opposite compound leaves; young twigs are filled with soft white pith.

species.name: Golden chanterelle
species.identify: Egg-yolk to apricot yellow, vase or trumpet shaped, with blunt forking false gills that run down the stem like melted wax. Smells of apricots.

species.name: Wild raspberries
species.identify: Compound berry that pulls free of its core, leaving a hollow thimble. Canes are prickly, leaves white-woolly underneath.

species.name: Salmonberry
species.identify: Tall arching canes with three leaflets, magenta flowers early, then a raspberry-shaped berry in salmon-orange to deep red.

species.name: Wild blueberries
species.identify: Low shrubs with small oval leaves; berries dusty blue with a five-pointed crown at the tip and green-white flesh inside. In the east it is the lowbush blueberry (V. angustifolium) of barrens and burns; in the western mountains and on the coast, the oval-leaf and bog blueberries, taller and picked the same way.

species.name: Huckleberries
species.identify: Waist-high shrubs, thin oval leaves, single dark purple berries in the leaf axils — one per stem, not in clusters.

species.name: Thimbleberry
species.identify: Large soft maple-shaped leaves, no thorns, white flowers, and a shallow, wide scarlet berry like a thimble that collapses when picked.

species.name: Prickly pear (tunas & nopales)
species.identify: Flat paddle cactus; the fruit (tuna) sits on the paddle rim and ripens deep magenta. Both fruit and young pads are used. Which prickly pear depends on where you are: Engelmann's in the desert Southwest (zones 8–11), the low plains and brittle prickly pears of the prairies and BC (hardy to zone 3), and the eastern prickly pear of sandy ground in the east (zones 5–9).

species.name: Wild blackberries
species.identify: Berry keeps its white core when picked (unlike raspberry). Thorny arching canes, five leaflets.

species.name: Chicken of the woods
species.identify: Overlapping fan-shaped brackets, bright orange on top, sulphur-yellow underneath with tiny pores — never gills.

species.name: Hen of the woods (maitake)
species.identify: A big grey-brown rosette of overlapping spoon-shaped fronds on a branching white stem, with pores underneath.

species.name: Giant puffball
species.identify: Smooth white ball, football-sized or larger. Slice it top to bottom: it must be pure white and uniform like a marshmallow, with no gills, no outline of a mushroom, no yellowing.

species.name: King bolete (porcini)
species.identify: Fat white stem with a fine raised net near the top, brown 'bun' cap, and a sponge of white-to-yellow pores that never stain blue.

species.name: Lobster mushroom
species.identify: Not a mushroom but a parasitic mould that turns its host bright orange-red and pimply, with firm white flesh inside. A strong fishy smell means it is old.

species.name: Matsutake (pine mushroom)
species.identify: White to buff, dense and heavy, with a distinctive cinnamon-and-gym-socks smell you can identify blindfolded. Gills white, with a partial veil.

species.name: Oyster mushroom
species.identify: Shelving clusters of oyster-shaped caps with white gills that run down a stubby off-centre stem or none at all. Faint anise smell.

species.name: Lion's mane
species.identify: A white pom-pom of soft downward-hanging spines, growing straight out of a tree trunk.

species.name: Wild hazelnuts
species.identify: Multi-stemmed shrub; nuts in clusters. American hazelnut (east and prairies) wraps each nut in ragged leafy husks; beaked hazelnut (the north and west) hides it in a long, bristly tube — wear gloves.

species.name: Black walnut
species.identify: Tennis-ball green husks lying under a tall tree with long compound leaves; the husk stains everything it touches brown.

species.name: Pawpaw
species.identify: Understorey tree with huge drooping leaves and green mango-shaped fruit; ripe ones fall and give to a gentle squeeze.

species.name: American persimmon
species.identify: Blocky alligator-hide bark; orange fruit the size of a plum, only ripe when it is wrinkled, squishy and usually on the ground.

species.name: Elderberries
species.identify: Flat, heavy clusters of tiny purple-black berries on red-tinged stems, on a shrub with opposite compound leaves.

species.name: Rose hips
species.identify: The red-orange fruit left after a wild rose blooms, topped with a dried five-pointed crown of sepals.

species.name: Staghorn sumac
species.identify: Upright, fuzzy, deep-red cone-shaped clusters on velvety branches. Red and upright is the rule.

species.name: Wild grapes
species.identify: Woody vine with shreddy bark and forked tendrils opposite the leaves; small purple-black grapes with seeds.

species.name: Highbush cranberry
species.identify: Maple-like three-lobed leaves and translucent scarlet berries in flat clusters, each with one flat stone.

species.name: Wild cranberries
species.identify: Thin trailing vines through the moss with tiny evergreen leaves; hard red berries sitting on top of the moss. The large cranberry (V. macrocarpon) is the one of eastern bogs; across the boreal north and the taiga it is the small cranberry (V. oxycoccos), pea-sized on even finer vines, picked the same way.

species.name: Chokecherry
species.identify: Long drooping clusters of dark red-to-black cherries on a small tree with finely toothed oval leaves.

species.name: Wild and abandoned apples
species.identify: An apple tree gone feral: small, spotty, often superb fruit. Every seedling tree is genetically unique.

species.name: Acorns
species.identify: Collect brown, freshly fallen nuts with no weevil holes; float them in water and discard the ones that swim.

species.name: Wild pecans
species.identify: Tall tree with long compound leaves; thin-shelled nuts in husks that split into four neat sections.

species.name: Shagbark hickory nuts
species.identify: Unmistakable bark peeling off in long vertical shaggy plates; husks split cleanly into four to release a pale, sweet nut.

species.name: Hawthorn berries
species.identify: Thorny small tree with lobed leaves and clusters of small red haws, each holding one to five hard stones. Cut one open to see the stones.

species.name: Wintergreen (teaberry)
species.identify: Ankle-high evergreen with thick glossy oval leaves and a bright red berry; crush a leaf and it smells exactly of wintergreen.

species.name: Salal
species.identify: Leathery, glossy, egg-shaped leaves on a knee-to-shoulder-high shrub; hairy dark blue-black berries in a row along a reddish stalk.

species.name: Sea grape
species.identify: Big round leathery leaves with red veins; grape-like clusters that ripen unevenly to purple.

species.name: Beach plum
species.identify: Low sprawling shrub in the sand, with dusty purple plums about the size of a marble.

species.name: Juniper berries
species.identify: Low spiky evergreen with needles in whorls of three, each with a white stripe on top; the 'berries' are fleshy blue cones that take two, sometimes three, years to ripen — so green and blue ones hang together.

species.name: Chaga
species.identify: A black, cracked, charcoal-like mass bursting out of a birch trunk, rusty orange-brown and corky inside.

species.name: Miner's lettuce
species.identify: Distinctive once mature: a round disc of leaf with the flower stalk coming up through the middle of it.

species.name: Wild fennel
species.identify: Tall feathery blue-green plant with an unmistakable anise smell, a smooth green stem and yellow umbels.

species.name: Broadleaf plantain
species.identify: A flat rosette of broad oval leaves with five or more deep parallel veins running end to end, and a narrow greenish flower spike. Tear a leaf slowly and the veins pull out as tough strings.

species.name: Yarrow
species.identify: Soft, flat, very finely divided ferny leaves — the species name means a thousand leaves — a solid hairy stem, flat-topped clusters of small white or pink flowers, and a strong sharp aroma when crushed.

species.name: Sheep sorrel
species.identify: Small arrow-shaped leaves with two backward-pointing lobes at the base, on a wiry reddish stem. Sharply lemony taste.

species.name: Lamb's quarters
species.identify: Goosefoot-shaped leaves with a mealy white bloom on the undersides that beads water; ridged stems, often red-streaked.

species.name: Purslane
species.identify: Prostrate mats of smooth red stems with fat, glossy, paddle-shaped succulent leaves. No hairs, no milky sap.

species.name: Burdock root
species.identify: Dig first-year plants — a rosette of huge rhubarb-like leaves, woolly and pale underneath, with no flower stalk yet.

species.name: Maple sap
species.identify: Sugar maple has five-lobed leaves with smooth-sided notches and grey furrowed bark. Any maple can be tapped; sugar and black maples run sweetest.

species.name: Wood sorrel
species.identify: Three heart-shaped leaflets that fold down at night, small yellow five-petalled flowers, and a sharp lemon taste.

species.name: Chickweed
species.identify: Sprawling mats with small opposite oval leaves and a single line of fine hairs running up one side of the stem, switching sides at each leaf pair. Stretch the stem: an elastic inner core.

species.name: Dulse
species.identify: Flat, hand-shaped, deep red-purple fronds with no midrib, attached by a small disc.

species.name: Wild rice
species.identify: Tall grass standing above the water with a branching seed head; grain is long, dark and slips free when ripe.

species.name: Garlic mustard
species.identify: Crush a leaf — it smells of garlic, and nothing that resembles it does. First-year rosettes have kidney-shaped, scallop-edged leaves; second-year stalks 30–100 cm (1–3 ft) carry triangular toothed leaves, small four-petalled white flowers and thin upright seed pods, over a white S-curved taproot.

species.name: Red clover
species.identify: Three oval leaflets each marked with a pale chevron, on hairy stems; round pink-purple flower heads 2–3 cm (about 1 in) across, each made of dozens of tiny pea flowers, sitting right above a pair of leaves.

species.name: Chicory
species.identify: Sky-blue flowers 3–4 cm (1–1½ in) across with square-ended, fringed petals, opening in the morning and closing by early afternoon, scattered up a stiff, nearly leafless, zigzag stem to 1.5 m (5 ft). A dandelion-like basal rosette with a bitter milky sap and a deep taproot.

species.name: Wild bergamot (bee balm)
species.identify: Square hairy stem 60–120 cm (2–4 ft) with opposite, toothed, lance-shaped leaves that smell strongly of oregano and thyme when rubbed, topped by a single shaggy round head of lavender-pink tubular flowers above a ring of pale bracts.

species.name: Ground ivy (creeping Charlie)
species.identify: Trailing square stems that root at every node; opposite, round-to-kidney-shaped leaves with scalloped edges on long stalks; small blue-violet two-lipped flowers in the leaf axils in spring; and a sharp minty-skunky smell when crushed.

species.name: Selfheal (heal-all)
species.identify: Square stem with opposite, oval to lance-shaped leaves that are barely toothed; and a stubby club-shaped flower head made of overlapping fringed bracts, with purple hooded flowers poking out a few at a time. The head stays on as a brown bristly knob long after flowering.

species.name: Wild mint (Canada mint)
species.identify: A square, usually hairy stem 20–60 cm (8–24 in) tall with opposite, toothed leaves and a strong, clean mint smell; the small pink-to-white flowers sit in tight whorls in the leaf axils up the stem, never in a spike at the top. If the flowers crown the stem, it is a different mint.

species.name: Goldenrod (Canada goldenrod)
species.identify: Stiff unbranched stems 1–1.5 m (3–5 ft) packed with alternate, lance-shaped, three-veined, toothed leaves and no basal rosette at flowering; a pyramidal plume of hundreds of tiny yellow flowers along the upper sides of arching branches. Insect-pollinated — its pollen is heavy and sticky and does not blow.

species.name: Pineapple weed (wild chamomile)
species.identify: A low, hairless, ferny-leaved plant 5–30 cm (2–12 in) tall with cone-shaped yellow-green flower heads that have no petals at all. Crush a head: it smells unmistakably of pineapple. No pineapple smell, no pineapple weed.

species.name: Common mallow (cheeseweed)
species.identify: Round, softly hairy, scalloped leaves with five to seven shallow lobes and a deep notch where the long stalk joins, on sprawling round stems from a tough taproot; small white-to-pale-pink five-petalled flowers with notched petals; and a flat fruit like a tiny wheel of cheese, split into a ring of wedge-shaped segments.

species.name: Wild carrot (Queen Anne's lace)
species.identify: A hairy, ribbed stem and leaves that smell exactly like carrot when crushed — both are required. In flower, a flat white umbel with a whorl of forked green bracts underneath and usually one dark purple floret in the centre; the old head curls into a bird’s nest.

species.name: Cow parsnip
species.identify: A huge native umbel plant, 1–3 m (3–10 ft), with a hollow, deeply ridged stem covered in soft hairs and no purple blotches; the leaves are enormous, three-parted and maple-like, up to 50 cm (20 in) across. Flat white flower heads 15–30 cm (6–12 in) wide in May–July.

species.name: Common milkweed
species.identify: A single thick, unbranched, downy stem 0.6–1.5 m (2–5 ft) tall with big opposite oval leaves, velvety underneath, and milky sap. Round, fragrant pink-mauve flower balls in June–July, then fat, warty, spindle-shaped pods.

species.name: Jerusalem artichoke (sunchoke)
species.identify: A rough, hairy sunflower 1.5–3 m (5–10 ft) tall with broad, sandpapery leaves on winged stalks, and flowers 5–9 cm (2–3.5 in) across with 10–20 narrow yellow rays around a yellow-green centre in August–October. Dig to confirm: knobbly tubers on short runners under the clump.

species.name: Wapato (arrowhead)
species.identify: Arrow-shaped leaves with two long basal lobes pointing backward and veins that radiate from where the stalk joins the blade; white three-petalled flowers in whorls of three on a separate leafless stalk, July–September. The tubers sit at the ends of long runners in the mud, up to 1 m (3 ft) from the plant.

species.name: Groundnut (hopniss)
species.identify: A twining herbaceous vine with milky sap — unusual in a pea — and leaves of 5–7 oval, pointed leaflets; dense clusters of fragrant maroon-brown pea flowers in July–September. Follow the thin root and you find tubers strung along it like beads on a cord.

species.name: Evening primrose
species.identify: A first-year rosette of long, narrow, slightly hairy leaves, each with a prominent white or pink midrib and often red flecks; the second-year stalk is 1–2 m (3–6 ft), reddish and hairy, with four-petalled yellow flowers that open at dusk and a cross-shaped stigma.

species.name: Watercress
species.identify: Hollow, hairless stems that float or sprawl and root at every node; pinnate leaves with 3–9 rounded leaflets, the end one largest; small white four-petalled flowers in April–July; and a clean mustard-pepper taste.

species.name: Wild sarsaparilla
species.identify: One leaf stalk rising from the ground and splitting into three branches, each with 3–5 finely toothed oval leaflets, so it looks like three leaves on one stem; a separate, shorter, leafless stalk underneath carries usually three round clusters of greenish-white flowers in May–June, then blue-black berries.

species.name: Sochan (cutleaf coneflower)
species.identify: Basal leaves deeply cut into 3–7 lobes like a turkey’s foot, on a smooth, hairless stem with a waxy blue-green bloom, 1–3 m (3–10 ft) tall. July–September flowers have 6–12 drooping yellow rays around a green cone that yellows as it ages.

species.name: Beechnuts
species.identify: Smooth, pale grey bark on a tall tree; long, sharp, cigar-shaped buds; oval leaves with coarse teeth and straight parallel veins, many held, bleached, through winter. The nuts are small, three-sided and come two to a soft-bristled husk that splits into four.

species.name: Eastern white pine
species.identify: Soft, flexible, bluish-green needles in bundles of five — the only eastern pine with five — and long, slender, curved cones with resin-tipped scales. Horizontal whorls of branches give old trees a layered look.

species.name: Black cherry
species.identify: A tall tree — the only cherry that grows to timber size — with young bark banded by horizontal pores and old bark broken into dark ‘burnt potato chip’ plates. Turn a leaf over: a line of rusty hairs runs along the base of the midrib. A snapped twig smells of bitter almond.

species.name: Wild plums
species.identify: A thorny shrub or small tree that flowers white before the leaves, with short spur branches ending in a sharp point. Fruit a true plum, 2–3 cm (1 in), red, orange or yellow with a whitish bloom and a single flattened stone.

species.name: Black locust flowers
species.identify: Only the flowers are food: hanging 10–20 cm (4–8 in) clusters of white, sweet-scented pea flowers in late May or June on a deeply furrowed tree with feathery compound leaves and a pair of short spines at the base of each leaf.

species.name: Redbud flowers
species.identify: Small magenta-pink pea flowers growing straight out of the bare twigs, branches and even the trunk in April or May, before the heart-shaped leaves open. Flat bean-like pods follow and hang on through winter.

species.name: Mayapple
species.identify: Knee-high colonies of one or two deeply lobed umbrella leaves per stalk; the two-leaved plants hold a single nodding white flower in the fork in spring and one egg-shaped fruit in summer. Only a soft, yellow, strongly fragrant fruit that comes away in your hand is ripe.

species.name: Spicebush
species.identify: A loose understory shrub with smooth-edged oval leaves and fine white dots on the twigs; scratch a twig and it smells sharply of lemon and allspice. Tiny yellow flowers hug the bare twigs in early spring, and female shrubs carry glossy red oval berries in September.

species.name: Sassafras
species.identify: Three leaf shapes on one tree — plain oval, three-lobed, and a one-thumbed ‘mitten’ — on green twigs that smell of root beer when scratched. Female trees carry dark blue berries in red cups in autumn.

species.name: Autumn olive
species.identify: A sprawling thorny shrub whose leaves flash silver underneath; in autumn it is weighed down with small red berries finely speckled with silver and brown scales, each with one soft seed.

species.name: Fireweed
species.identify: A tall unbranched spire, 1–2 m (3–6 ft), of four-petalled magenta flowers opening from the bottom up; narrow alternate leaves on a round, often reddish stem. Hold a leaf to the light: the side veins curve and join into a line running just inside the edge, which no look-alike shares.

species.name: Lingonberry (partridgeberry)
species.identify: A creeping evergreen 5–20 cm (2–8 in) tall with small, thick, glossy oval leaves whose edges roll under; turn a leaf over and look for scattered dark bristly dots on the pale underside. Firm red berries hang in small clusters at the branch tips, and the tiny bell flowers that preceded them had four fused petals.

species.name: Cloudberry (bakeapple)
species.identify: A single stalk 10–25 cm (4–10 in) tall with two or three rounded leaves of five to seven shallow lobes, one white five-petalled flower, and one berry — no thorns, no canes. The berry starts hard and red and ripens to soft, translucent amber, which is the only stage to pick.

species.name: Labrador tea
species.identify: A knee-high evergreen shrub whose leathery, alternate leaves have edges rolled under and a thick rusty-orange wool on the underside — dense, felted and unmistakable on mature leaves. White flowers in rounded clusters in June. No rusty wool, no Labrador tea.

species.name: Bunchberry
species.identify: A 10–20 cm (4–8 in) plant with a single whorl of four to six oval leaves whose veins arch toward the tip like a dogwood’s; in June the four white ‘petals’ are bracts around a knot of tiny flowers, and by August a tight bunch of bright red berries sits in the middle of the whorl.

species.name: Wild currants and gooseberries
species.identify: A shrub 1–2 m (3–6 ft) tall with maple-like lobed leaves, and berries that each keep a dried flower ‘tail’ at the tip. Currants are thornless with six or more berries in a dangling chain; gooseberries carry spines at the leaf nodes and hold one to four berries, often bristly.

species.name: Nodding onion
species.identify: A clump of flat, grass-like leaves from a slender bulb, and in July–August a stem that bends sharply at the top so the pink umbel of bell flowers hangs downward. Crush a leaf: the whole plant smells strongly of onion. No onion smell means it is not an onion, whatever else it looks like.

species.name: Camas
species.identify: Grass-like basal leaves and an upright spike of starry six-petalled blue to violet flowers in April–June; the bulb below is a plain white onion-shape with no smell. Mark plants while they are in flower and dig only those — the bulb alone cannot be told from death camas.

species.name: Oregon grape
species.identify: An evergreen shrub with holly-like pinnate leaves of five to nine spiny-edged leaflets, upright clusters of yellow flowers in spring, and powdery blue-black berries in grape-like bunches by late summer. Scrape a stem: the inner bark and wood are bright yellow.

species.name: Pinyon pine nuts (piñon)
species.identify: A short, rounded, often multi-trunked pine 3–9 m (10–30 ft) tall with stiff needles in twos (single-leaf pinyon has them singly); small round cones 4–5 cm (1½–2 in) with thick scales that open in September–October to drop large, thin-shelled brown seeds.

species.name: Wild garlic (ramsons)
species.identify: Broad, bright green, smooth-edged leaves up to 25 cm (10 in) long, each on its own slender stalk straight from the ground, and a strong garlic smell from every crushed leaf. From April, round heads of white star-shaped flowers on a leafless stalk.

species.name: Mediterranean wild asparagus
species.identify: An evergreen, scrambling clump of stiff, sharply pointed, needle-like ‘leaves’. After the winter rains, thin dark green to purplish spears — pencil-thin or thinner — push up through last year’s prickly tangle.

species.name: Common sorrel
species.identify: Arrow-shaped leaves whose two base lobes point straight back, a thin papery sheath where each leaf meets the stem, and a sharp lemon-sour taste. In early summer, slender spikes of tiny reddish flowers up to 60 cm (2 ft) tall.

species.name: St George’s mushroom
species.identify: A stocky, white to cream mushroom with a thick, smooth cap 5–15 cm (2–6 in) across, crowded narrow white gills, a fat stem with no ring, a white spore print, and a strong smell of wet flour or cucumber. It is up in spring, when few large pale mushrooms are.

species.name: Yellow morel
species.identify: A pale cream to yellow-brown, sponge-like cap of irregular pits with paler ridges, joined to the stem at its lower edge. Slice it top to bottom: one continuous hollow from cap tip to stem base.

species.name: Birch sap
species.identify: Silver birch has white, papery bark that cracks into black diamonds at the base and drooping twig tips; downy birch has duller bark and upright, downy twigs. Both are tapped. The sap runs for a few weeks in early spring, before the leaves open.

species.name: Elderflower (European elder)
species.identify: A woody shrub or small tree with corky, furrowed grey-brown bark and opposite leaves of five to seven toothed leaflets; flat, creamy-white heads of tiny five-petalled flowers up to 24 cm (9 in) across, with a heavy sweet scent.

species.name: Sweet cicely
species.identify: A soft, downy, fern-like plant to 1–2 m (3–6 ft) with finely divided pale green leaves, often flecked white, and a strong sweet smell of aniseed when crushed. White flower heads in April–June, then long, slender, ridged seeds 15–25 mm (⅝–1 in), green at first and glossy dark brown when ripe.

species.name: Marsh samphire
species.identify: A low, leafless, jointed succulent 10–30 cm (4–12 in) tall, like a tiny branching cactus: bright glassy green, very salty, and it snaps cleanly. It turns red or purple in autumn.

species.name: Sea beet (wild spinach)
species.identify: A sprawling, leafy perennial with dark green, glossy, leathery leaves — the lower ones wavy-edged and roughly triangular — often on reddish stems, and in summer thick, grooved spikes of tiny green flowers. It looks and tastes like a wild chard.

species.name: Woodland strawberry
species.identify: Three shiny, toothed leaflets on hairy stalks; white five-petalled flowers whose rounded petals touch; and small red berries about 1 cm (⅜ in) long with the seeds on the surface. On the end leaflet, the tip tooth is as long as or longer than the teeth beside it.

species.name: Chanterelle (girolle)
species.identify: Egg-yolk yellow, firm and solid, with a wavy cap and blunt, forking ridges — not true gills — running down the stem like melted wax. Pale flesh inside, a fruity apricot smell, and it grows from the soil, never from wood.

species.name: Bilberry
species.identify: A knee-high shrub with bright green, angled stems and small, finely toothed oval leaves. Blue-black berries with a dusty bloom hang one per stalk, each with a little crown at the tip — and the flesh is purple-red right through, staining fingers and tongue.

species.name: Rowan berries
species.identify: A slim tree with smooth silvery-grey bark and feathery leaves of many toothed leaflets in pairs; big flat clusters of scarlet-orange berries, each about 1 cm (⅜ in) across with a tiny black five-pointed star at the tip.

species.name: Sea buckthorn
species.identify: A thorny shrub with narrow, silvery-grey, willow-like leaves and branches packed with bright orange berries 6–8 mm (¼ in) across, from late summer into winter. Only female bushes fruit.

species.name: Elderberries (European elder)
species.identify: Drooping, flat-topped clusters of glossy purple-black berries 6–8 mm (¼ in) across on purple-red stalks, on a woody shrub with corky bark and opposite compound leaves.

species.name: Cornelian cherry
species.identify: A shrub or small tree that covers itself in clusters of tiny yellow flowers in February and March, long before the leaves. Leaves opposite, oval and smooth-edged; in late summer, glossy, oblong red fruits about 2 cm (¾ in) long, each with one stone.

species.name: Saffron milk cap
species.identify: A carrot-orange cap with darker concentric rings, inrolled at first and later funnel-shaped, on a short, often hollow stem. Break it and it bleeds carrot-orange milk; bruised and handled parts slowly turn green.

species.name: Parasol mushroom
species.identify: Big and tall: a cap 10–25 cm (4–10 in) across, pale with coarse brown scales and a dark central bump; a slender stem up to 40 cm (16 in) with brown snakeskin banding; a thick double-edged ring that slides up and down; free white gills and a white spore print.

species.name: Black trumpet (horn of plenty)
species.identify: A thin, hollow, sooty grey-black trumpet up to 10 cm (4 in) tall, cap and stem all one piece; the outer surface is paler ash-grey and smooth or faintly wrinkled, with no gills.

species.name: Hedgehog mushroom
species.identify: A buff, apricot or pale orange cap, often lumpy and irregular, with soft, crowded, pale spines hanging underneath instead of gills, and firm white flesh that bruises orange.

species.name: Yellowfoot (winter chanterelle)
species.identify: A small brown funnel-shaped cap 1–4 cm (½–1½ in) across, often with a hole down the middle, on a hollow, yellow to orange stem; underneath, pale greyish-yellow forked ridges, not gills, running down the stem.

species.name: Sloes (blackthorn)
species.identify: A dense, very thorny shrub with dark bark and white blossom on bare black twigs in early spring, before the leaves. In autumn, round blue-black fruits about 1 cm (⅜ in) across with a waxy blue bloom, each holding one stone.

species.name: Sweet chestnut
species.identify: A big tree with long, glossy leaves edged with sharp, regular teeth, and bark that twists in spiralling ridges on old trunks. The nuts come in twos and threes inside a husk covered in dense, needle-sharp spines; each is glossy brown, flat on one side, with a pointed tuft at the tip.

species.name: Strawberry tree (arbutus)
species.identify: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy, toothed leaves and red-brown, peeling bark. Round, warty red fruits 1.5–2 cm (⅝–¾ in) across ripen in autumn at the same time as the next year’s clusters of creamy, bell-shaped flowers.

species.name: Baobab (fruit and leaves)
species.identify: A vast, swollen grey trunk with smooth, folded bark and stubby branches that look like roots, bare of leaves for most of the dry season. The leaves are hand-shaped, with five to seven finger-like leaflets. The fruit is a velvety, egg- to sausage-shaped pod up to 25 cm (10 in) long on a long hanging stalk: a hard woody shell around chalky, off-white pulp and black kidney-shaped seeds.

species.name: Marula
species.identify: A single-stemmed tree with a broad, spreading crown and grey, mottled bark. Leaves are divided into pairs of leaflets with one at the tip, bunched at the ends of the branches. The plum-sized fruits, 3–4 cm (1½ in) long, fall while still green and turn pale yellow on the ground; inside is white, juicy flesh around a hard, thick-walled stone holding two or three kernels. Only female trees bear fruit.

species.name: Tamarind
species.identify: A big, dense, evergreen tree with feathery leaves of many small paired leaflets (no single leaflet at the tip) and small yellow flowers streaked with orange or red. The fruit is a brown, slightly curved pod with a thin, brittle shell over sticky, brown, sweet-sour pulp and one to six glossy brown seeds; African pods are the short kind.

species.name: Monkey orange (green monkey orange)
species.identify: A small, often spiny tree with opposite, rounded, glossy leaves showing three to five veins running from the base. The fruit is large, round and hard, with a woody shell that turns from green (often speckled) to yellow as it ripens; inside, many hard brown seeds packed in sweet-sour, brown, edible pulp.

species.name: Sycamore fig
species.identify: A big, spreading tree with yellowish to orange bark that peels in papery strips, and rough, heart-shaped leaves with prominent yellow veins beneath. The figs, 2–3 cm (about 1 in) across, grow in thick clusters on short leafless branchlets from the trunk and main branches and ripen from greenish-buff to yellow or reddish. Broken twigs bleed milky latex.

species.name: Shea fruit
species.identify: A medium-sized tree with thick, corky bark deeply cracked into squares, white latex where it is cut, and long, leathery, oblong leaves crowded in tufts at the branch tips. The fruit looks like a large plum, 4–8 cm (1½–3 in) long, with a thin layer of sweet green pulp around one big, glossy brown seed — the shea 'nut'.

species.name: African star apple (agbalumo, udara)
species.identify: A forest tree with milky latex. The fruit is round with a smooth skin that ripens from green to orange, yellowish-peach or burnt orange; cut across, the seeds sit in a five-pointed star in sticky, sweet-sour pulp.

species.name: Desert date (balanites)
species.identify: A spiny tree up to about 10 m with long, straight, green spines arranged in a spiral, and dark green leaves of two small leaflets growing from the base of the spines. The date-like fruit is under 4 cm (1½ in) long, green when unripe, ripening yellow to pale brown, with a brittle skin over sticky, bittersweet pulp and one very hard stone.

species.name: Eru (okazi, fumbwa)
species.identify: A slender climbing vine up to about 10 m long with thick, glossy, leathery, oval leaves about 8 cm (3 in) long, pointed at the tip. It is a gymnosperm, related to the conifers: no true flowers, but small cone-like spikes, and on female vines fleshy seeds 1–1.5 cm long that ripen red-orange.

species.name: Amaranth greens (morogo, mchicha)
species.identify: Upright or sprawling herbs, often with reddish stems, carrying alternate, oval to diamond-shaped, smooth-edged leaves on long stalks, and dense, bristly spikes of tiny green or reddish flowers at the top and in the leaf joints. No milky sap, no berries, no trumpet flowers. Spiny amaranth has a pair of sharp spines at each leaf base.

species.name: Spider plant (cat's whiskers)
species.identify: An upright, branching annual up to about 1.5 m with a sticky, glandular stem and a strong smell. Leaves are hand-shaped, of three to seven (usually five) finely toothed leaflets. The flowers are white or purple-tinged with four clawed petals, and the purple stamens and the ovary are held out on a long stalk well beyond the petals — the cat's whiskers. Pods are long, thin and beaked.

species.name: Num-num (Natal plum)
species.identify: A dense, evergreen shrub with glossy, leathery, dark green leaves in opposite pairs, sharp forked (Y-shaped) thorns, and white milky sap from any broken leaf or twig. Flowers are white five-petalled stars, scented most strongly at night. The fruit is a large, oval, glossy red berry with soft red flesh; flowers and fruit are often on the bush together.

species.name: Sour fig (suurvy)
species.identify: Trailing mats of fat, three-angled, finger-like succulent leaves, often reddish at the tips. Big many-petalled flowers 6–15 cm (2½–6 in) across, yellow and fading to pale pink. The fruit is a fleshy, top-shaped capsule about 35 mm (1⅜ in) across that turns from green to yellow and smells sweet when ripe.

species.name: Waterblommetjie (Cape pondweed)
species.identify: Long-stalked, narrow-oval leaves floating flat on the water, and above them forked white flower spikes shaped like a 'Y', each branch lined with white petal-like bracts and dark purple-brown stamens, sweetly scented. The plant dies back as the pools dry in summer and regrows with the autumn rain.

species.name: Kei apple
species.identify: A dense, viciously thorny shrub or small tree with straight spines 3–6 cm (1–2½ in) long and clusters of small oval leaves at their base. Male and female flowers are on separate plants, so only some bushes fruit. The fruit is a round, apricot-coloured berry 2.5–4 cm (1–1½ in) across, the same yellow-orange inside and out, with several small seeds.

species.name: Wild garlic (Tulbaghia)
species.identify: Clumps of narrow, grey-green, strap-like leaves up to about 60 cm (2 ft), and on bare stalks above them loose heads of tubular lilac-mauve flowers from midsummer into autumn. Leaves and flowers smell strongly of garlic when bruised — and that smell is the test.

species.name: Termite mushrooms (omajowa)
species.identify: It grows out of a termite mound or the ground over a termite nest, never from wood. The cap usually has a pointed nipple at its centre, and the stem tapers into a long, tough root (pseudorhiza) that runs down — sometimes a metre or more — to the termites' fungus garden. Sizes run from a few centimetres (Termitomyces microcarpus, in crowds) to frying-pan caps of 15–40 cm (T. schimperi) and, in T. titanicus, up to a metre across.

species.name: Kalahari truffle
species.identify: A roundish, potato-like fungus growing just under the sand, up to 12 cm (4¾ in) across and usually under 200 g (7 oz). It gives itself away by lifting the sand into a little mound with cracks in the surface. Cut through, it is solid right through — no gills, no stem, no hollow.

species.name: Sorrel (suring)
species.identify: A low, almost stemless plant with clover-like leaves of three heart-shaped leaflets, each notched at the tip, on long stalks. Bright yellow, funnel-shaped flowers with a whitish tube stand above the leaves in loose heads of three to twenty on bare stalks, from about June to October. Leaves and stalks taste sharply sour.

species.name: Dune spinach (duinespinasie)
species.identify: A sprawling, trailing undershrub with thick, pale stems and fat, oval, saddle-shaped leaves 1–6 cm (½–2½ in) long that sit straight on the stem without a stalk and glisten as if wet — the sheen comes from tiny water-storage cells. Small yellow four-petalled flowers sit in groups of three to five in the upper leaf joints from August to November, followed by thickly four-winged fruit.

species.name: Cape gooseberry (golden berry)
species.identify: A soft, spreading, velvety-hairy shrub up to about 1 m (3 ft) with heart-shaped, wavy-edged leaves. The drooping, bell-shaped flowers, 1–2 cm (½–¾ in) across, are yellow with dark purple-brown blotches inside. Each fruit is a smooth, round, golden-orange berry 1.25–2 cm (½–¾ in) across, like a tiny tomato, enclosed in a papery, ten-ribbed husk — a small lantern — that dries from green to straw-brown.

species.name: Wild rosemary (kapokbos)
species.identify: A bushy, evergreen, silvery-grey shrub up to about 1 m (3 ft) with small, narrow, needle-like leaves in tufts along the branches — fleshier on plants near the sea — that smell of camphor, like Vicks, when crushed. In autumn and winter it covers itself in small flowers of two or three white petals round a purple centre, followed by seed heads wrapped in long white hairs like cotton wool: kapok is the Afrikaans for snow.

species.name: Mussels (rock mussels)
species.latin: Mytilus spp., Choromytilus meridionalis, Perna perna
species.identify: Paired, wedge-shaped shells, pointed at the hinge end and rounded at the other, anchored in clusters by tough threads (the byssus, or beard). Blue and Mediterranean mussels are blue-black, purple or brownish and grow to about 14 cm (5½ in); the Cape's black mussel is narrower, glossier and blacker; the brown mussel is brown.

species.name: Sea lettuce
species.identify: Bright to dark green, translucent, crumpled sheets up to about 30 cm (12 in) across and only two cells thick — like wet green tissue paper — fixed by a tiny disc, with no stalk.

species.name: Sea bamboo (Cape kelp)
species.identify: South Africa's largest kelp, up to 12–15 m (40–50 ft) long: a root-like holdfast, a single long, hollow, gas-filled stalk and, at the surface, a large bulb carrying a tangle of thick, strap-like fronds. Washed up, it lies on the sand like brown hosepipe with a bulb at one end.

species.name: Rock samphire (sea fennel)
species.identify: A hairless, cushion-forming perennial 15–50 cm (6–20 in) tall with ridged, solid stems and very fleshy, grey-green leaves divided into narrow, almost cylindrical lobes; crushed, they smell resinous and lemony. Flat umbels of small yellow-green flowers from June to September are followed by spongy, ribbed, egg-shaped fruit.

species.name: Carrageen (Irish moss)
species.identify: A small, tough, springy red seaweed up to about 22 cm (9 in), in tufts from a disc-shaped holdfast. A narrow, unbranched stalk widens into flat fronds that fork up to five times into a fan with rounded tips. The colour runs from deep purple-red to green or yellow in strong sun, and under water the tips often shine blue-violet.

species.name: Sea purslane
species.identify: A low, straggling, much-branched shrub up to about 80 cm (2½ ft) on sprawling, woody stems. The leaves are thick, untoothed and oval to elliptical, in opposite pairs, silvery grey-green and mealy to the touch. From July to September, short spikes of tiny greyish flowers with yellow stamens appear at the tips.

species.name: Alexanders
species.identify: A stout, hairless biennial up to 1.5 m (5 ft). The glossy, yellowish- to dark green leaves are divided into broad, bluntly toothed leaflets, and the stems are solid when young, becoming hollow and grooved with age. From April to June it carries dense, rounded umbels of yellow-green flowers with no sepals, followed by seeds that turn from green to black in July and August.

species.name: Caper
species.identify: A sprawling shrub with long, trailing stems, thick, shiny, round to oval leaves and usually small curved thorns. The showy flowers last a single day: four white to pinkish petals and a burst of long violet stamens. Before they open they are small, round green buds — the capers. Left on the plant, they become plump green fruit on long stalks, the caper berries.

species.name: Carob (St John's bread)
species.identify: A broad, round-crowned evergreen tree up to 15 m (50 ft) with leaves 10–20 cm (4–8 in) long, divided into pairs of leaflets. Small flowers grow straight from the trunk and old branches in autumn. The pods are flat, leathery and slightly curved, 10–30 cm (4–12 in) long, ripening from green to dark brown, sweet-smelling, with 10–13 very hard seeds. Most trees are male or female, and only females bear pods.

species.name: Myrtle (mirto)
species.identify: A dense evergreen shrub up to 5 m (16 ft) with small leaves 2–5 cm (¾–2 in) long in opposite pairs, fragrant with essential oil when crushed. Its white or pink-tinged flowers have five petals and a brush of many stamens. The berries change colour in late summer and ripen from November into the new year to blue-black.

creatures.name: Walleye
creatures.identify: Olive-gold flanks, a spiny first dorsal, and the big glassy eye that gives it the name and lets it hunt in low light.

creatures.name: Smallmouth bass
creatures.identify: Bronze-brown with vertical bars, red eye, and a jaw that ends level with the eye — not past it.

creatures.name: Largemouth bass
creatures.identify: Green with a dark lateral stripe, and an upper jaw that extends past the back of the eye.

creatures.name: Northern pike
creatures.identify: Long torpedo body, duck-like jaws, light bean-shaped spots on a dark green flank.

creatures.name: Muskellunge
creatures.identify: Like a pike but with dark bars on a light flank — the reverse pattern — and pointed tail lobes.

creatures.name: Lake trout
creatures.identify: Pale cream spots on a dark green-grey body, and a deeply forked tail.

creatures.name: Brook trout
creatures.identify: Called speckled trout (and omble de fontaine) in much of Canada. Worm-like pale vermiculations on a dark green back, red spots ringed in blue, and white-edged lower fins.

creatures.name: Rainbow trout
creatures.identify: A pink-red band down the flank, small black spots over the whole body and tail.

creatures.name: Brown trout
creatures.identify: Butter-brown flanks with black and red spots ringed in pale halos; few or no spots on the tail.

creatures.name: Yellow perch
creatures.identify: Golden-yellow with five to eight (usually about seven) dark vertical bars and orange lower fins.

creatures.name: Black crappie
creatures.identify: Silvery with irregular black speckling, a deep flat body and seven or eight dorsal spines.

creatures.name: Bluegill
creatures.identify: Deep round body, a solid black ear flap, and a small mouth.

creatures.name: Channel catfish
creatures.identify: Deeply forked tail, scattered dark spots on young fish, and long whiskers.

creatures.name: Chinook salmon
creatures.identify: Black gums at the base of the teeth, small black spots on both tail lobes, and real size — often over 10 kg on the Pacific, smaller in the Great Lakes.

creatures.name: Coho salmon
creatures.identify: White gums, spots only on the upper tail lobe, and a bright silver body turning deep red in the river.

creatures.name: Steelhead
creatures.identify: A sea-run or lake-run rainbow: chrome-bright, small black spots, a faint pink stripe that brightens in the river.

creatures.name: Atlantic salmon
creatures.identify: Sparse X-shaped black spots above the lateral line, a slim wrist to the tail, and no spots on the tail.

creatures.name: Striped bass
creatures.identify: Silver with seven or eight unbroken horizontal black stripes, and a large mouth.

creatures.name: Arctic grayling
creatures.identify: An enormous sail-like dorsal fin flecked with turquoise and red, over a silver-purple body.

creatures.name: Lake whitefish
creatures.identify: Small, blunt, overhanging snout above a small mouth; silver body, deeply forked tail.

creatures.name: Burbot
creatures.identify: Eel-like tail, mottled brown-yellow skin, and a single barbel on the chin.

creatures.name: Redfish (red drum)
creatures.identify: Copper-bronze with at least one black spot at the base of the tail, and an underslung mouth.

creatures.name: Speckled trout (spotted seatrout)
creatures.identify: Silver-grey with distinct round black spots on the back and tail, and two prominent canine teeth.

creatures.name: Snook
creatures.identify: A sharp black lateral line running right through the tail, and a sloping forehead over a protruding lower jaw.

creatures.name: Pacific halibut
creatures.identify: A huge diamond-shaped flatfish, both eyes on the dark right side, with a crescent-shaped tail.

creatures.name: Lingcod
creatures.identify: A big mottled head full of teeth, long body, and flesh that is sometimes bright blue-green (harmless — it cooks white).

creatures.name: Kokanee
creatures.identify: A landlocked sockeye: bright silver in summer, turning brilliant red with a green head to spawn.

creatures.name: European perch
creatures.identify: Five to eight dark bars on a greenish flank, bright red-orange lower fins, and a spiny first dorsal fin with a black blotch at the back.

creatures.name: Zander
creatures.identify: Slim and glassy-eyed, with grey-brown saddles, rows of black spots on the spiny dorsal fin, and long fang-like canine teeth.

creatures.name: Common carp
creatures.identify: Big bronze scales (or the scattered big scales of a mirror carp), a long dorsal fin, and two pairs of barbels at a rubbery, tube-like mouth.

creatures.name: Tench
creatures.identify: Olive-green and very slimy, with tiny scales, small red-orange eyes, rounded fins, and one small barbel at each corner of the mouth.

creatures.name: Roach
creatures.identify: Silver with a blue-green back, bright red eyes, reddish lower fins, and a dorsal fin set directly above the pelvic fins.

creatures.name: Common bream
creatures.identify: Deep, flat-sided and slimy; bronze as an adult (silvery when young), with a long anal fin and a mouth that shoots out into a tube.

creatures.name: Barbel
creatures.identify: Long and muscular with a flat belly, an underslung mouth with four barbels, and a bronze back over a pale belly.

creatures.name: Chub
creatures.identify: Thick-set and broad-headed with a big white-lipped mouth, large dark-edged scales in a net pattern, and a convex, reddish anal fin.

creatures.name: European grayling
creatures.identify: A tall, sail-like dorsal fin flecked with purple and red, silver-grey flanks with scattered dark spots, and a small mouth set low.

creatures.name: Arctic char
creatures.identify: Pale pink-to-cream spots on a dark back, a belly that turns brilliant red-orange at spawning, and white-edged lower fins.

creatures.name: Wels catfish
creatures.identify: Huge and scaleless, with a broad flat head, two long whiskers and four short ones under the chin, a tiny dorsal fin, and an anal fin that runs almost to the tail.

creatures.name: European whitefish
creatures.identify: Silver and herring-like, with a small head, a short snout over a small mouth, big scales, an adipose fin and a deeply forked tail.

creatures.name: European sea bass
creatures.identify: Silver-grey and streamlined, with two separate dorsal fins (the first spiny), a large mouth, and a sharp spine on the gill cover.

creatures.name: Gilthead seabream
creatures.identify: A deep, oval, silver body with a golden bar between the eyes, a dark spot high on the gill cover, and a red edge to the gill cover.

creatures.name: Atlantic mackerel
creatures.identify: Torpedo-shaped, with wavy black tiger stripes on a blue-green back, a plain silver-white belly, and a row of small finlets before the forked tail.

creatures.name: Pollack
creatures.identify: Bronze-green to olive back, a dark lateral line that curves up over the pectoral fin, and a jutting lower jaw with no chin barbel.

creatures.name: Atlantic cod
creatures.identify: A pale, curving lateral line, a single barbel on the chin, three dorsal fins, and a speckled olive-brown back.

creatures.name: European eel
creatures.identify: Snake-like and slimy with tiny buried scales, one long fin running round the tail, and a lower jaw that juts past the upper.

creatures.name: Nile perch
creatures.identify: A huge silver perch with a blue sheen, a dorsal fin cut deeply into spiny and soft halves, a rounded tail, and a dark eye ringed in bright yellow.

creatures.name: Nile tilapia
creatures.identify: Deep-bodied and grey-brown with faint bars, and the tell: regular dark vertical stripes right across the tail fin. Breeding males turn reddish, especially on the fins.

creatures.name: Mozambique tilapia (blue kurper)
creatures.identify: Deep-bodied and dull silvery-olive with a few dark blotches along the side and no regular stripes on the tail. Breeding males turn black with a white throat, red-edged fins and a pointed, duck-bill snout.

creatures.name: Tigerfish
creatures.identify: Silver with dark horizontal stripes along the upper sides, a red-orange tail edged in black, and big fang-like teeth that overlap the jaws even with the mouth shut.

creatures.name: Goliath tigerfish
creatures.identify: A heavy, silver-grey tigerfish with a thick, tuna-like body, a black adipose fin and enormous dagger-like teeth — the largest of all the tigerfish.

creatures.name: Sharptooth catfish (barbel)
creatures.identify: A long, eel-like body, a flat bony head, four pairs of whiskers, and one very long dorsal fin with no small fatty fin behind it. Dark grey to olive above, white below.

creatures.name: Vundu
creatures.identify: A massive olive-brown catfish with whiskers long enough to reach the belly fins, and a fatty (adipose) fin behind the dorsal that is almost as long as the dorsal itself.

creatures.name: Smallmouth yellowfish
creatures.identify: A big, streamlined, bronze-gold barb with large scales, golden fins and a small mouth.

creatures.name: Largemouth yellowfish
creatures.identify: A yellowfish built for hunting: a longer, heavier head and a big mouth. The largest scaled fish native to southern Africa.

creatures.name: Dusky kob (kabeljou)
creatures.identify: A long, silvery-bronze drum with a coppery head, a big mouth, and in life a row of pale spots along the lateral line.

creatures.name: Galjoen
creatures.identify: A deep, short, heavily scaled fish with thick lips and spiny fins; black among the rocks and silver-bronze over sand, changing colour almost instantly.

creatures.name: Snoek
creatures.identify: Long, thin and steel-blue, with a black membrane on the long first dorsal fin, small finlets behind the fins, and fang-like teeth.

creatures.name: Yellowtail (Cape yellowtail)
creatures.identify: A big, torpedo-shaped jack: dark blue above and white below with a sharp line between, a yellow-bronze stripe along the side, and a bright yellow tail.

creatures.name: Giant trevally (GT)
creatures.identify: A thick, powerful jack with a steep, blunt head, hard scutes along the base of the tail, and silver-grey to black colouring; mature males can be almost black.

creatures.name: Giant African threadfin
creatures.identify: A big silver fish with a pointed, see-through snout, a bright yellow pectoral fin with four long white threads beneath it, and a deeply forked tail.

creatures.name: Bluefish (elf, shad)
creatures.identify: Blue-green above and silver below, with a big head, a jutting lower jaw and a single row of knife-edged teeth. The short, spiny first dorsal fin folds into a groove and runs straight into the long second one, and there are no finlets before the forked tail.

creatures.name: White steenbras (pignose grunter)
creatures.identify: A big, silvery seabream with a mother-of-pearl sheen, a pointed nose and a small mouth — tiny teeth at the front, crushing molars behind. Young fish carry dark crossbars that fade with age.

creatures.name: Hottentot seabream (Cape bream)
creatures.identify: A small, deep-bodied, bronze-grey to brownish seabream with a yellowish eye, a distinct lateral line, small dark fins and a small mouth lined with incisor teeth. Young fish are dusky brown.

creatures.name: White musselcracker (brusher)
creatures.identify: A heavy, silver-grey seabream with darker fins, a white belly and massive jaws: four incisor-like teeth at the front of each jaw, the middle two enlarged and curved. In the water it shows a bluish glow.

creatures.name: Leerfish (garrick)
creatures.identify: A long, deep, flattened jack, brown above and silver-white below, with a pointed snout and a wildly wavy lateral line that curves up over the pectoral fin and dips behind it. The tips of the dorsal and anal fins are black; it has no hard scutes on the tail.

creatures.name: Spotted grunter
creatures.identify: Dark grey above, silver-white below, with many small brown spots over the back, sides and dorsal fin but not the head, a dark spot on the edge of the gill cover, and a small mouth with thick lips. Young fish have no spots.

creatures.name: White seabream (blacktail)
creatures.identify: A deep, oval, silver seabream with a big black saddle on the tail stalk. Mediterranean fish carry nine alternating dark and pale bars and a black spot above the pectoral fin; large Cape blacktail are plain silvery-grey, with only faint bars on the young.

creatures.name: Red roman
creatures.identify: A vivid orange seabream with a broad, concave forehead, a blue bar between the eyes and a white, saddle-like mark on the back below the middle of the dorsal fin.

creatures.name: Cape kurper
creatures.identify: A small fish, yellow to golden-brown with dark markings that run onto the dorsal and anal fins. Breeding males turn darker, with vertical bars and blackened fins and lower jaw.

creatures.name: Common dentex
creatures.identify: A big, oval, flat-sided seabream with rows of strong canine teeth, the front ones largest. Young fish are grey with black spots on the back; they turn pink as they mature, and old fish are bluish-grey with the spots faded.

creatures.name: Flathead grey mullet (striped mullet)
creatures.identify: A stout, round-bodied fish with a broad, flat head, a thin upper lip and a clear, fatty eyelid that covers most of the eye. Olive-green above, silver on the sides, often with six or seven dark stripes along the flank; it has no visible lateral line.

creatures.name: Garfish
creatures.identify: Long and thin, bluish-green above with a silver-grey belly, both jaws drawn out into a narrow beak lined with widely spaced teeth, and the dorsal and anal fins set well back on the body. The bones are green.

creatures.name: Ballan wrasse
creatures.identify: A heavy, deep-bodied wrasse with a big head, thick, wrinkled lips, a long spiny dorsal fin and large scales. Colour varies from plain green or brown to red-brown covered in pale spots.

creatures.name: Black seabream
creatures.identify: An oval, grey-silver seabream with a small head and mouth, faint lengthwise lines and six to nine dark vertical bars, and no dark spots. Males guarding nests turn almost black.

creatures.name: European flounder
creatures.identify: An oval flatfish, usually with both eyes on the right side, dull brown or olive above with darker blotches and sometimes reddish spots, pearly white below. The skin is rough, with rows of prickly bumps along the lateral line and the bases of the fins.

creatures.name: Great barracuda
creatures.identify: A long, pike-like fish with a big, pointed head, a jutting lower jaw and fang-like teeth. Blue-grey above and silver below, with dark oblique bars on the upper side that stop short of the lateral line, scattered black blotches low on the flank, and a dark tail with white tips.

creatures.name: Atlantic tarpon
creatures.identify: A huge, deep silver fish with very large, armour-like scales, a big upturned mouth with a long bony plate in the lower jaw, and a last dorsal ray drawn out into a long filament that nearly reaches the tail.

creatures.name: Couta (narrow-barred Spanish mackerel)
creatures.identify: A long, blue-grey and silver mackerel covered in many thin, wavy vertical bars, with rows of finlets before the tail and a lateral line that drops sharply below the end of the second dorsal fin.

creatures.name: Crevalle jack (jack crevalle)
creatures.identify: A deep, heavy jack with a steep, blunt head, olive to blue-green above and silvery to brassy below, a black spot on the edge of the gill cover, another at the base of the pectoral fin and a row of hard scutes along the rear of the lateral line. The chest is bare except for a small patch of scales in front of the pelvic fins, and the anal-fin lobe and the underside of the tail stalk are yellow.

creatures.name: West African ladyfish
creatures.identify: A slim, round-bodied, bright silver fish with a large mouth, a bony plate between the arms of the lower jaw, a single dorsal fin in the middle of the back and a deeply forked tail. The scales are small — 72 to 83 along the lateral line — and there is no long trailing ray on the dorsal fin.

creatures.name: Blackchin tilapia
creatures.identify: A small, deep-bodied tilapia, silvery with blue, gold or orange tints, with dark blotches on the chin and throat of adults, a dark rear edge to the gill cover, dark tips to the soft rays of the dorsal fin and irregular spots or faint bars along the sides.

creatures.name: Cassava croaker
creatures.identify: A long, silvery-grey croaker with a big, oblique mouth, a slightly jutting lower jaw and a pair of large canine teeth at the front of the upper jaw. Rows of small dark spots follow the scale rows, the spiny dorsal fin has a black tip, the tail is pointed and the inside of the gill cover is black.

creatures.name: Gorean snapper
creatures.identify: A stocky red snapper with a pointed head, a steep forehead and big eyes: vermilion on the back, pink in large fish, fading to white below, with a thin blue line — whole or broken into spots — from the upper jaw under the eye to the corner of the gill cover. Young fish are plain brownish.

creatures.name: Silver catfish (bagrid catfish)
creatures.identify: A grey to silvery catfish with a pointed snout, four pairs of barbels, a stiff, sharp spine at the front of the dorsal fin and of each pectoral fin, a small fleshy fin before the tail and a forked tail whose upper lobe is longer than the lower.

creatures.name: Milkfish
creatures.identify: A long, streamlined, silvery fish with a small, toothless mouth, a single, sail-like dorsal fin in the middle of the back, long sickle-shaped pectoral fins and a big, deeply forked tail. Olive green on the back; the fins have dark edges.

creatures.name: Mangrove red snapper (river snapper)
creatures.identify: A heavy snapper, greenish-brown to bronze on the back and reddish on the sides — fish from deep water are red all over — with a silvery or whitish belly and prominent canine teeth. Young fish carry about eight pale bars on the sides and two blue lines across the cheek.

creatures.name: Talang queenfish (largemouth queenfish)
creatures.identify: A long, flat-sided, silvery fish, blue-grey on the back, with a single row of large, oval dark blotches along or just above the lateral line, a big mouth whose upper jaw reaches past the eye, a deeply forked tail and semi-detached, finlet-like rays at the back of the dorsal and anal fins. The skin feels like leather: its tiny scales are buried in it.

creatures.name: Spangled emperor
creatures.identify: A deep, yellowish-bronze emperor with a long, sloping snout and thick lips, a white or pale blue spot at the centre of many scales and three blue streaks or rows of blue spots running forward and down from the eye. The fins are whitish to yellow and the dorsal fin is edged red; there is no red on the gill cover.

creatures.name: Honey bee
creatures.identify: Golden-brown, banded, furry thorax, and pollen packed onto the hind legs in visible baskets.

creatures.name: Bumble bees
creatures.identify: Big, round and very furry, in black with yellow, orange or white bands.

creatures.name: Mason bee
creatures.identify: Small, dark metallic blue-black, carrying pollen dry on the underside of the abdomen rather than on the legs.

creatures.name: Hoverfly
creatures.identify: Wasp-striped but a true fly: two wings not four, huge eyes, and it hovers dead still in mid-air.

creatures.name: Monarch butterfly
creatures.identify: Orange with heavy black veins and a white-spotted black border. The caterpillar is banded yellow, white and black.

creatures.name: Swallowtail butterflies
creatures.identify: Large, with tails on the hindwings. Swallowtails are the family Papilionidae; the common ones here are all in the genus Papilio — eastern and Canadian tiger swallowtails (P. glaucus, P. canadensis) with black-and-yellow stripes, the black swallowtail (P. polyxenes) with rows of yellow and blue spots, the western tiger (P. rutulus) and the big giant swallowtail (P. cresphontes).

creatures.name: Ruby-throated hummingbird
creatures.identify: Tiny, iridescent green above; the male has a black-looking throat that flares ruby in the right light.

creatures.name: Lady beetle
creatures.identify: The adult everyone knows; the larva is the useful one — a spiky, alligator-shaped grey-and-orange creature that looks like a pest.

creatures.name: Green lacewing
creatures.identify: Delicate pale green adult with lacy wings and gold eyes. Eggs sit singly on the ends of hair-thin stalks.

creatures.name: Praying mantis
creatures.identify: Long green or brown body, triangular head that swivels, and folded raptorial front legs.

creatures.name: Ground beetle
creatures.identify: Shiny black or bronze, fast-running, with grooved wing covers and long legs.

creatures.name: Braconid wasp
creatures.identify: A tiny, harmless, thread-waisted wasp. The cocoons on a caterpillar's back are the unmistakable sign.

creatures.name: Garden orb weaver
creatures.identify: Striking black and yellow, with a heavy zig-zag band of silk down the middle of the web.

creatures.name: Earthworm
creatures.identify: Familiar; look for the saddle-like clitellum a third of the way down a mature worm.

creatures.name: Aphids
creatures.identify: Tiny pear-shaped insects, green, black or pink, with two little tailpipes at the rear. Sticky honeydew and ants tending them are the giveaway.

creatures.name: Tomato hornworm
creatures.identify: A very large green caterpillar with white chevrons and a stiff horn at the rear. It hides in plain sight.

creatures.name: Cabbage white
creatures.identify: A plain white butterfly with one or two black wing spots. The caterpillar is velvety green and lies along a leaf vein.

creatures.name: Colorado potato beetle
creatures.identify: A round beetle with ten black stripes on a cream back; orange egg clusters and fat pink humpbacked larvae underneath the leaves.

creatures.name: Squash bug
creatures.identify: A flat grey-brown shield-shaped bug; bronze egg clusters laid in neat V patterns in the angle of leaf veins.

creatures.name: Squash vine borer
creatures.identify: The adult is a day-flying orange-and-black moth that looks like a wasp. The damage is sudden wilting plus sawdust-like frass at the stem base.

creatures.name: Japanese beetle
creatures.identify: Metallic green body with copper wing covers and small white tufts along the sides. Leaves are skeletonised to lace.

creatures.name: Slugs
creatures.identify: The silvery slime trail and ragged holes in the middle of leaves, not at the edges.

creatures.name: Cucumber beetle
creatures.identify: Small and yellow with three black stripes down the back, or with twelve spots.

creatures.name: Flea beetle
creatures.identify: Tiny shiny black beetles that jump like fleas when disturbed, leaving leaves peppered with shot-holes.

creatures.name: Spider mites
creatures.identify: Leaves take on a fine bronze stippling; fine webbing appears in the leaf axils. Tap a leaf over white paper to see the moving specks.

creatures.name: Cutworms
creatures.identify: Fat grey-brown caterpillars that curl into a tight C when you dig them up. A seedling severed cleanly at ground level is the sign.

creatures.name: Earwig
creatures.identify: Slim brown insect with a pair of pincers at the rear.
